HF 2697.raw_text:
An Act relating to the payment of pecuniary damages,
restitution, and prosecution costs.
BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF IOWA:
Section 1. Section 910.2, Code 2026, is amended by adding
the following new subsection:
NEW SUBSECTION. 3. Notwithstanding any other statute
or rule of law, with the consent of the defendant and the
prosecuting attorney, the court may order as part of the
dismissal of a public offense that the defendant pay pecuniary
damages to the victim, category “B” restitution, which shall
include court costs, and prosecution costs under section
815.13.
EXPLANATION
The inclusion of this explanation does not constitute agreement with
the explanation’s substance by the members of the general assembly.
This bill relates to the payment of pecuniary damages,
restitution, and prosecution costs.
The bill provides that notwithstanding any other statute
or rule of law, with the consent of the defendant and the
prosecuting attorney, the court may order as part of the
dismissal of a public offense that the defendant pay pecuniary
damages to the victim, category “B” restitution, which shall
include court costs, and prosecution costs.

Amend House File 2697 as follows:
1. Page 1, line 6, after <offense> by inserting <or
violation of an ordinance>
2. Page 1, by striking lines 8 and 9 and inserting <include
court costs.>

Section 1. Section 910.2, Code 2026, is amended by adding
the following new subsection:

HF 872.raw_text:
An Act relating to the maximum annual gross income for an
enterprise to qualify as a targeted small business.
BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF IOWA:
Section 1. Section 15.102, subsection 12, paragraph a, Code
2025, is amended to read as follows:
a. “Targeted small business” means a small business any
enterprise which is fifty-one percent or more owned, operated,
and actively managed by one or more women, minority persons,
service-disabled veterans, or persons with a disability
provided the business enterprise meets all of the following
requirements:
(1) Is located in this state.
(2) Is operated for profit and under a single management.
(3) Has either fewer than twenty employees or an annual
gross income of less than four ten million dollars computed as
an average of the three preceding fiscal years.
EXPLANATION
The inclusion of this explanation does not constitute agreement with
the explanation’s substance by the members of the general assembly.
This bill relates to the maximum annual gross income for
an enterprise to qualify as a targeted small business. Under
the bill, an enterprise must have an annual gross income of
less than $10 million to qualify as a targeted small business.
Under current law, the maximum is $4 million.

HCR 105.raw_text:
A Concurrent Resolution to provide for the business
of the first extraordinary session of the 2026
legislative session.
WHEREAS, Governor Kim Reynolds has convened an
extraordinary session of the Ninety-first General
Assembly on Friday, October 2, 2026; NOW THEREFORE,
BE IT RESOLVED BY THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES,
THE SENATE CONCURRING, That pursuant to Joint Rule 3,
the business of the first extraordinary session of
the 2026 legislative session shall be limited to the
consideration of a bill for an Act relating to the
major economic growth attraction program and including
effective date provisions; and any other resolutions
that either chamber may adopt.

SF 2342.raw_text:
An Act relating to the required beneficiary and use of a public
officer insurance policy.
BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF IOWA:
Section 1. Section 64.3, subsection 4, Code 2026, is amended
by striking the subsection.
EXPLANATION
The inclusion of this explanation does not constitute agreement with
the explanation’s substance by the members of the general assembly.
Under current law, certain public officers are required to
obtain a bond that runs to the state for the use and benefit
of any corporation, public or private, or person injured or
sustaining loss, with a right of action in the name of the
state for its or the corporation’s or person’s use (Code
section 64.18). In 2024, the general assembly enacted a
provision allowing public officers to obtain an insurance
policy in lieu of such a bond. The state is required to be the
beneficiary of the insurance policy and the policy is required
to be for the use and benefit of any corporation, public or
private, or person injured or sustaining loss, with a right of
action in the name of the state for its or the corporation’s
or person’s use (Code section 64.3(4)). This bill strikes
these requirements for an insurance policy obtained in lieu of
a bond.

Amend Senate File 2342 as follows:
1. Page 1, after line 2 by inserting:
<Sec. ___. EFFECTIVE DATE. This Act, being deemed of
immediate importance, takes effect upon enactment.>
2. Title page, line 2, after <policy> by inserting <, and
including effective date provisions>
3. By renumbering as necessary.
